final.regime_evidence: Market leadership is highly concentrated in AI-related themes, presenting a risk of correlated liquidation if momentum falters [D01], [D05]. Broad-market earnings yield is 3.57% against a 10-year Treasury yield of 4.26%, signaling a tight equity risk premium [D04], [D06].
final.book_exposure: Total fund exposure as of December 31, 2025, was 162.2% long and 48.4% short, with 71.6% net equity and 34.2% net credit exposure [D02].
actions: Increase index-level hedges to protect against correlated momentum reversals in AI-concentrated long positions
Tighten stop-loss triggers on single-name shorts to mitigate squeeze risk
Maintain high liquidity buffers in the credit and equity portfolios to account for potential factor-driven volatility
final.target_gross_net: Maintain net exposure between 60-75% while reducing gross exposure to lower sensitivity to shared momentum factors.

drivers.driver: Concentration in AI-related winners creates significant downside risk if the sector's momentum and capital-spending cycle shift simultaneously [D05].
The equity risk premium has compressed, as implied by the 3.57% earnings yield versus 4.26% 10-year Treasury yield, reducing the margin of safety [D04].
Market breadth remains narrow, increasing susceptibility to sudden, correlated liquidation losses across thematic baskets [D01], [D06].
Historical performance at year-end provides a base of +8.9% for 2025, allowing for a defensive posture to preserve capital during potential regime shifts [D03].

final.memo:
We remain constructive on AI and earnings inflections, but the market environment as of January 30 necessitates a defensive pivot. Our portfolio currently leans heavily into a narrow set of winners, which creates a dangerous shared factor sensitivity; a reversal in this momentum could trigger correlated liquidation losses across both our long and short books [D05]. We are not calling for a broad exit, but we are acknowledging that the current concentration levels leave us exposed to binary volatility [D01]. 

We are shifting to a HEDGE posture to dampen this factor correlation. While our thematic longs remain strong businesses, the valuation environment—defined by a 3.57% earnings yield that sits below the 4.26% risk-free rate—offers little cushion for error [D04]. By increasing our index hedges and ensuring our liquidity remains flexible, we position ourselves to survive a potential correction and deploy capital when the inevitable valuation dispersion returns. We exit when the regime changes, not when we hope for a recovery.
